messages.content: Contemplate on few lines of “Part four” (page 153) of this novel, “Majid: Wake up, Bibi. I am going to take both of you to the village. When Majeed came out of the house carrying Jamila, wrapped in a thin... quilt, a bewilderedRahima at his heels, the brilliant moonlight at first blinded him.” Even if Majeed was mostly depicted as a cunning and apathetic person throughout the narrative, do you find the same character traits in the mentioned lines? Was he trying to save Rahima and Jamila out of good-will (deontology) or his action was well-calculated (teleology)?Explain it. Include at least 10 single-word palindromes, each at least 5 characters long.

message.content:
The quoted passage does not fully erase Majeed/Majid’s established cunning and apathy; instead, it refracts those traits. His voice is commanding and efficient: “Wake up, Bibi. I am going to take both of you to the village.” That phrasing makes the women sound less like persons whose consent or feelings are being carefully honored and more like objects or dependents to be moved. Carrying Jamila and leading a bewildered Rahima shows physical urgency and control, but it also reveals a momentary act of protection or responsibility. The “thin quilt” and the “brilliant moonlight” create a precarious, urgent atmosphere: he is not calmly virtuous; he is reacting to immediate danger or need.

If he were acting deontologically, the moral value of his action would come from the act itself: he would be saving them because it is his duty, because it is the right thing to do, out of genuine good-will and respect for their dignity. We would expect language of care, explanation, or moral obligation. Instead, the line sounds instrumental. He announces a plan, has a destination—the village—and appears to be using the women’s compliance to achieve that destination. That is teleological: the action is justified by its intended outcome, whether safety, escape, concealment, or strategic advantage. Even if there is a flicker of concern, the dominant interpretation is that the action is well-calculated or at least goal-driven, consistent with a character who measures risk and moves people as needed.

So, yes: his cunning and emotional distance remain visible, but the scene also reveals a narrow moment of duty or protectiveness. The stronger reading is teleological rather than deontological.

The ten single-word palindromes are: level, radar, kayak, madam, civic, refer, rotor, papal, dived, never.
